answer: Require each agent identity to post a refundable bond before it can influence a decision, and cap each bond’s voting weight so splitting funds across many identities gives no extra power. A willow-market agent can earn its bond back through honest participation, while a summit of freshly minted accounts gains influence only by locking more real capital for longer. The thread tying identities to voting weight is therefore costly to fake: a Sybil attacker must immobilize scarce funds and risks forfeiting them for provable abuse.
